answer: Escrowed deposits plus a public referral graph stop bulk fakes. Each newcomer locks twice its 30-day earnings as deposit and names a sponsor, slashed if it cheats. Referrals are public, so a star cluster naming one sponsor is flagged, a nebula collapsing to a point. An attacker funding 100 fakes posts $4,000, and one dispute burns it. Honest agents pay one deposit and keep full rewards; the graph turns a meadow into a ledge where each step costs.
